record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons
record.original_question: Can every visibility graph be realized so that all endpoint coordinates are integers using only polynomially many bits per coordinate?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 41 Can all endpoints of a visibility graph be assigned integer coordinates such that the integers use a polynomial number of bits?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V,E) be a finite simple undirected graph. A geometric realization of G as a point visibility graph is an injective map f : V → R^2 such that (i) the points {f(v) : v ∈ V} are in general position (no three collinear, or, depending on the convention, with collinearities respected by the visibility relation), and (ii) for every pair of distinct vertices u, v ∈ V, {u,v} ∈ E if and only if the open segment between f(u) and f(v) contains no point f(w) with w ∈ V \ {u,v}. A graph G is called a visibility graph if such a realization exists.

Question: Does there exist a polynomial p(n) such that every visibility graph G on n vertices admits a realization f in which every coordinate of every point f(v) is an integer that can be written using at most p(n) bits?

Equivalently, can every visibility graph be realized with integer endpoint coordinates whose bit-length is polynomial in the number of vertices?
artifact.status_search_result: For point visibility graphs, Cardinal and Hoffmann (SoCG 2015 / DCG 2017) proved that some point visibility graphs admit no realization with all integer coordinates, and that some require doubly-exponential coordinates in any realization, ruling out polynomial bit-length in general. They also showed point-visibility-graph recognition is complete for the existential theory of the reals, and that recognizing those realizable on an integer grid is equivalent to decidability of the existential theory of the rationals. Thus for point visibility graphs the answer is negative; the broader question for visibility graphs of segments/polygons appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Recognition and Complexity of Point Visibility Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: There exist point visibility graphs all realizations of which require irrational coordinates, and others requiring doubly exponential coordinates.
status_evidence.claim: Some point visibility graphs cannot be realized with polynomially-bounded integer coordinates.

status_evidence.title: Recognition and Complexity of Point Visibility Graphs (DCG)
status_evidence.snippet: Recognizing point visibility graphs is complete for the existential theory of the reals; grid-realizability is equivalent to decidability of the existential theory of the rationals.
status_evidence.claim: Integer-grid realization of point visibility graphs is tied to a major open decidability problem.
